findings.issue_text: Imported external HTML stored with cook_method: raw_html bypasses Discourse's sanitization pipeline, and is emitted via <%= raw post.cooked %> in embed/best.html.erb, causing stored XSS in the Discourse origin
The url from external feed data is interpolated unescaped into an HTML attribute (<a href='#{url}'>), enabling attribute/HTML injection into the raw-HTML post body
request.referer is interpolated directly into an inline <script> block in embed.html.erb without escaping; an attacker controlling the referer path/query can inject script into the Discourse origin
postMessage uses the full referer (including path) as targetOrigin, which per spec must match the exact origin, so the resize message never arrives and iframe auto-resize is broken
$redis.setnx followed by a separate $redis.expire is not atomic; a crash between the two leaves a key with no TTL, permanently throttling that embed_url; should use SET key val NX EX 60
import does check-then-create with no uniqueness retry, so two concurrent imports of the same URL race and one raises RecordNotUnique, crashing the job and skipping the item for an hour
CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element, aborting the whole poll run and leaving remaining items unprocessed
feed_key is defined but never used; the feed-modified tracking it implies is missing, so every feed item is re-hashed and passed through TopicEmbed.import on every hourly run
open(url).read has no timeout, no size limit, and open-uri follows redirects to arbitrary hosts, allowing workers to hang, memory exhaustion, or SSRF that bypasses the host check
discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl; the check should be strict equality or a strict prefix comparison against the parsed origin

The attacker-controlled embed URL is used directly in TopicRetriever/open, letting any visitor with a matching referer trigger arbitrary server-side fetches of unbounded paths with no rate limit other than the 60s per-URL throttle, which path diversity defeats
document.getElementById('discourse-comments') result is used without a null check, throwing a TypeError on pages that include embed.js without the div
The loading page reloads every 30 seconds unconditionally, looping forever on permanent retrieval failure instead of showing an error
Adding force: true to an already-shipped migration is dangerous: re-running the migration drops and recreates the table, destroying data; existing migrations should not be edited
perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire feed poll (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})) inline instead of just enqueueing the poll job

Tests only stub poll_feed and never exercise the actual feed parsing/import path (missing link/content, Atom id fallback, relative-URL feeds); there is also no test for TopicEmbed.import_remote or the absolutize_urls port-nonstandard case

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported external HTML stored with cook_method: raw_html bypasses Discourse's sanitization pipeline, and is emitted via <%= raw post.cooked %> in embed/best.html.erb, causing stored XSS in the Discourse origin

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff explicitly introduces a `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html`, and `Post#cook` now short-circuits to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and feeds it `contents` from RSS (`PollFeed` uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no HTML sanitization) or from remote readability extraction. `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href/src` and does not sanitize tags/attributes. Finally, `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders the content as HTML via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any stored HTML (including potentially `<script>` or event-handler attributes from RSS content) would be emitted from the Discourse origin, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The url from external feed data is interpolated unescaped into an HTML attribute (<a href='#{url}'>), enabling attribute/HTML injection into the raw-HTML post body

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the `url` taken from feed/remote input is only checked with `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other attribute-breaking characters. That `url` is then interpolated directly into an HTML attribute using single quotes: `"#{url}"` and appended to `contents`. Since imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `:raw_html`, this HTML is rendered without the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Therefore, a crafted URL like `http://example.com/' onclick='alert(1)` would pass the regex and inject attributes/HTML into the raw post body.

adjudication_records.issue_text: $redis.setnx followed by a separate $redis.expire is not atomic; a crash between the two leaves a key with no TTL, permanently throttling that embed_url; should use SET key val NX EX 60

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code throttles with `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two Redis operations are not atomic; if the process crashes or is terminated after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will be left without a TTL. Subsequent calls will see the key and treat it as “retrieved recently” forever, effectively permanently throttling that embed_url until the key is manually deleted. Using a single atomic SET with NX+EX (or a Lua script/multi) would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import does check-then-create with no uniqueness retry, so two concurrent imports of the same URL race and one raises RecordNotUnique, crashing the job and skipping the item for an hour

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, enters a transaction that eventually calls `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so two concurrent imports for the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race to `create!`; the loser will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or equivalent) and there is no rescue/retry logic in this method. In the scheduled feed job (`Jobs::PollFeed`) retries are explicitly disabled (`sidekiq_options retry: false`), so such an exception would fail the run and the next attempt would indeed be at the next hourly recurrence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key is defined but never used; the feed-modified tracking it implies is missing, so every feed item is re-hashed and passed through TopicEmbed.import on every hourly run

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined to build a Redis key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but it is never referenced anywhere in the diff. The `poll_feed` method always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each`, calling `TopicEmbed.import(...)` for every item on each run. While `TopicEmbed.import` may no-op updates when `content_sha1` matches, the job still re-processes each item (including digesting contents inside `TopicEmbed.import`) every hour because no last-modified/etag/redis tracking is actually used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The attacker-controlled embed URL is used directly in TopicRetriever/open, letting any visitor with a matching referer trigger arbitrary server-side fetches of unbounded paths with no rate limit other than the 60s per-URL throttle, which path diversity defeats
document.getElementById('discourse-comments') result is used without a null check, throwing a TypeError on pages that include embed.js without the div

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `comments` is assigned via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then immediately used as `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no null/undefined guard. If a page includes `embed.js` but does not contain an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a `TypeError` at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The loading page reloads every 30 seconds unconditionally, looping forever on permanent retrieval failure instead of showing an error

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` contains a script that always calls `document.location.reload()` after 30000ms, with no max retries or failure detection. `EmbedController#best` renders `loading` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil (and only enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`), so if retrieval permanently fails (bad URL/content, network issues, job errors, etc.), the page will keep reloading indefinitely instead of ever surfacing an error state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding force: true to an already-shipped migration is dangerous: re-running the migration drops and recreates the table, destroying data; existing migrations should not be edited

adjudication.rationale: The diff edits an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table before recreating it. Modifying an already-committed migration like this introduces a data-loss hazard for anyone re-running/redoing/resetting migrations (or running the migration on a DB where `top_topics` already exists), and changing old migrations is generally unsafe practice compared to adding a new corrective migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire feed poll (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})) inline instead of just enqueueing the poll job

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, the code intentionally calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, and then immediately re-checks whether the requested `@embed_url` now exists (`return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`). That control flow depends on synchronous execution; simply enqueueing the poll job would not populate the embed before the subsequent existence check, changing behavior. Also, this call happens from a background job (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic`) in the provided diff, not directly in a web request. So while it may be debatable from an architectural/perf standpoint, the finding asserts it’s a defect that it’s not enqueued, which is not a clearly verifiable “real problem” from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests only stub poll_feed and never exercise the actual feed parsing/import path (missing link/content, Atom id fallback, relative-URL feeds); there is also no test for TopicEmbed.import_remote or the absolutize_urls port-nonstandard case

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior in Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed (SimpleRSS.parse(open(...)), link vs id fallback, i.content.scrub/CGI.unescapeHTML, and TopicEmbed.import calls), but the only added spec (spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb) tests only the gating in #execute and stubs expectations that poll_feed is/ isn’t called—there are no tests that exercise parsing/import behavior. Likewise, TopicEmbed.import_remote is newly added and used (e.g., in disqus.thor and TopicRetriever#fetch_http) but there is no spec covering import_remote’s Readability/open() path. TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls is covered only for default ports; there’s no test for the nonstandard-port branch (adding :port when not 80/443). These are all verifiable omissions in the added test suite.
